label: Roam Research
description: Query and write blocks and pages in a Roam Research graph via its official Backend API.
usage_notes: Base: `https://api.roamresearch.com/api/graph/{graph_name}/`; read with `POST .../q` (EDN Datalog in `{"query": ...}`, returns `{"result": [[...], ...]}`) or `.../pull`, write with `POST .../write`. Send `Authorization: Bearer {api_token}` and `Content-Type: application/json`. `/write` takes one object: `{"action": "create-page", "page": {"title": ...}}` or `create-block` with `"location": {"parent-uid": ..., "order": "last"}`; batch as `{"action": "batch-actions", "actions": [...]}` (a bare array is rejected). Good writes: 200, empty body. Calls answer 308 to a peer host whose subdomain and port vary; clients drop the header on it, so re-send to `Location` with the header re-attached, only if its host ends in `.api.roamresearch.com`; else stop. `You are not authenticated`: the header was dropped. `graph_name` is case-sensitive. To check a connection, read with `/q`; never write. `You don't have read access` means a miscased graph name, a bad token, or an append-only token; in the same cell, `POST https://append-api.roamresearch.com/api/graph/{graph_name}/append-blocks` with `{"location": {"page": {"title": "x"}}, "append-data": []}`. 403: bad name or token. 400 with `Invalid request` (expected: the token works): append-only, it can only add blocks there (`append-data`: `[{"string": ..., "children": [...]}]`), never read or edit. When checking a connection, that 400 is a pass though no data comes back: call `report_success` now; try nothing else. `You don't have write access` with working reads means a read-only token: writes need a new read & edit token, so tell the user.

form.title: Connect Roam Research
form.subtitle: Paste a graph API token to connect one Roam Research graph. What Anton can do with it is fixed by the token's access scope: read & edit, read-only, or append-only. Roam has no OAuth, so this is the only supported connection method.

methods.label: Graph API Token
methods.description: Paste a graph API token and the graph's name. Use a read & edit token if you want Anton to write.
methods.how_to:
## Generate a Roam Research graph API token

Roam's Backend API is authenticated per-graph with a static API token — there's no OAuth flow to connect your account as a whole, so you connect one graph at a time.

### Steps

1. Open the Roam graph you want Anton to access at [roamresearch.com](https://roamresearch.com).
2. Click **Settings** (bottom of the left sidebar), then open the **Graph** tab.
3. Scroll to the **API tokens** section and click **+ New API Token**.
4. Give it a name like `Anton`, choose an **Access Scope** (see the notes below; **read & edit** gives Anton the most to work with), and confirm.
5. Copy the token shown — it will not be displayed again.
6. Paste it into **API Token** below, and enter the **Graph name** exactly as it appears in your Roam URL (`roamresearch.com/#/app/<graph-name>`) — it is **case-sensitive**, so `MyGraph` and `mygraph` are not interchangeable.

### Notes

- The token only works against the ONE graph it was created in — connect each graph separately if you use more than one.
- Creating API tokens may require a paid Roam plan (Pro or Believer); free graphs may not show the API tokens section.
- An idle graph can take a few seconds to "wake up" on the first request after being closed — a slow first call is normal, not a broken token.
- Roam tokens are **scoped**, and the scope is fixed when you create the token. The dialog's **Access Scope** dropdown offers *read-only*, *read & edit*, and *append-only*:
  - **read & edit**: Anton can search, read, create and update pages and blocks. Pick this unless you have a reason not to.
  - **read-only**: Anton can search and read your graph, but any write fails with `You don't have write access to <graph>`.
  - **append-only**: Anton can only add new blocks to a page or your daily note, through Roam's Append API (beta). It cannot read, search or edit anything, including what it just added.
- A token's scope cannot be changed after creation. To give Anton more access, create a new token with the scope you want and reconnect.
- Rate limited by Roam (exact quota undocumented) — if you see frequent failures, space out requests.
